perspective:
Available to me as Bradley Ochoa:

- I am a salesperson at a marketing firm. Katherine Lasiloo is my colleague and the marketing manager. We have a professional relationship and have disagreed over traditional sales methods versus digital marketing.
- In our meeting, I presented data/charts from our last five campaigns to support traditional sales. I told Katherine I appreciated her digital strategies but believed traditional methods were being overlooked and better for core sales.
- I heard Katherine say the market is evolving, digital outreach has potential, and ask how I reconcile my data with rising online engagement. I said I was not suggesting abandoning digital, but was frustrated that proven methods were sidelined. She said she understood, wanted balance, and suggested analyzing data together to integrate both.
- Later, Katherine shared recent digital campaign success stories with increased engagement and sales. I felt uncertain, asked how those strategies are developed, and heard her explain targeting the right audience/message and offer to walk through analytics and decision-making. I admitted my doubts and wanted to understand more. She said adapting to market trends matters and suggested diving deeper into data.
- I proposed a joint strategy session to combine traditional and digital approaches. Katherine agreed, said combining strengths could improve results, and suggested scheduling brainstorming/next steps. I said I was hopeful and appreciated her collaboration; she said she looked forward to it.
- After a successful joint meeting, I worked overtime on a board presentation draft integrating both our ideas. I showed it to Katherine and said I was excited and wanted to nail it. She praised it as comprehensive and well thought out and suggested reviewing/fine-tuning again.
- After the board presentation succeeded and the new strategy was implemented, I felt grateful for my professional growth and our collaboration. I thanked Katherine and proposed regular strategy sessions. She said it was a pleasure, that my openness helped the partnership, and agreed to regular sessions.
